title: Password Security & Management Risk Calculator
metaDescription: Calculate your password security risk score. Assess weak passwords, reuse patterns, and missing 2FA to improve your digital security.
description: Evaluate your password security practices and identify vulnerabilities. This calculator assesses password strength, reuse patterns, authentication methods, and security habits to provide a comprehensive risk score and actionable recommendations.

inputs.helpText: Include email, social media, banking, shopping, and work accounts

inputs.helpText: Count distinct passwords, not variations of the same password

outputFields.label: Password Security Risk Score
outputFields.description: Overall security risk from 0 (highest risk) to 100 (lowest risk)

outputFields.label: Password Reuse Rate
outputFields.description: Percentage of accounts likely using duplicate passwords

formula: const reuseRate = Math.max(0, (totalAccounts - uniquePasswords) / totalAccounts * 100); let baseScore = 50; if (passwordManager === 'yes') baseScore += 25; else if (passwordManager === 'partial') baseScore += 10; if (twoFactorAuth === 'all') baseScore += 20; else if (twoFactorAuth === 'most') baseScore += 15; else if (twoFactorAuth === 'few') baseScore += 5; if (passwordComplexity === 'high') baseScore += 15; else if (passwordComplexity === 'medium') baseScore += 8; else baseScore -= 5; if (breachChecking === 'regularly') baseScore += 10; else if (breachChecking === 'sometimes') baseScore += 5; baseScore -= (reuseRate * 0.3); const riskScore = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, baseScore)); let riskLevel; if (riskScore >= 80) riskLevel = 'A - Excellent'; else if (riskScore >= 70) riskLevel = 'B - Good'; else if (riskScore >= 60) riskLevel = 'C - Fair'; else if (riskScore >= 40) riskLevel = 'D - Poor'; else riskLevel = 'F - Critical'; return { riskScore: Math.round(riskScore), riskLevel, reuseRate: Math.round(reuseRate) };

educational.methodology: This calculator evaluates password security based on industry best practices including unique password usage, authentication factors, complexity standards, and breach monitoring. The scoring system weighs password managers and 2FA most heavily as they provide the greatest security improvements.
tips: Use a reputable password manager like Bitwarden, 1Password, or Dashlane to generate and store unique passwords for every account
Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) on all important accounts, especially email, banking, and social media
Check if your accounts have been compromised using services like Have I Been Pwned
Use a privacy-focused browser for sensitive browsing to prevent password and session theft
Regularly update passwords for accounts that don't support 2FA or have been involved in data breaches
